To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose an extension of the Prototypical Networks for intent detection meta-learning that relies on unsupervised paraphrasing to limit overfitting on each episode, and that we show that this method is the state of art for intent detection metalearning, at no extra labelling effort, and without the need of a fine tuned conditional language model on each application domain.
we propose a novel meta learning algorithm for intent detection, based on Prototypical Networks and paraphrasing.
we propose ProtAugments: a novel extension of the Prototypical Networks that limits overfiting on the bias introduced at each meta learning iteration, by introducing diverse paraphrasing.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (i) how to leverage the power of language modeling in meta learning for few shot text classification, (ii) how to introduce diversity in the paraphrasing process to improve the generalization ability of the model, (iii) how to introduce paraphrasing without extra labeling efforts.
the following questions: 1) What are the benefits of unsupervised paraphrasing for few shot intent detection?
the following research question: can we use unsupervised paraphrasing to improve intent detection meta learning?

our method is the state of art method for short text intent detection meta learning with no extra labeling efforts.

ProtAugment is an unsupervised paraphrasing method for short texts classification that is the state of art in the intent detection meta learning task, at no extra annotation costs and with no need to fine tune the paraphrasing language model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we introduce a new unsupervised paraphrasing method that is used to improve the performance of intent detection meta learning.
ProtAugment is able to leverage the paraphrasing power of large language models for meta learning, and it does so in an unsupervised manner.
ProtAugment is an unsupervised meta learning algorithm for few shot intent detection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the diversity of paraphrased texts is a powerful inductive bias that can be leveraged for few shot learning.
unsupervised paraphrasing can be leveraged for intent detection, a task where the few shot classification objective is known to suffer from overfitting.
diverse paraphrasing can be used to improve the performance of a Prototypical Network on few-shot intent detection tasks.
